slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Blueprint copy: each student gets a triangle and must make an exact copy for a partner across the room using only compass and straightedge. No rulers.

  • I can copy a triangle with compass and straightedge by SSS and by SAS.
  • I can justify each copy by naming the three equalities and the test.

geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Blueprint copy: each student gets a triangle and must make an exact copy for a partner across the room using only compass and straightedge. No rulers.

  • I can copy a triangle with compass and straightedge by SSS and by SAS.
  • I can justify each copy by naming the three equalities and the test.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: a compass carries lengths, so congruence tests become recipes.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Copy a triangle by SSS (adapted from Construction 5, Jacobs p. 171).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Draw a ray and mark DE equal to AB.Compass copy of a segment.
Draw a circle centered at D with radius AC.DF will equal AC.
Draw a circle centered at E with radius BC.EF will equal BC.
Pick one crossing point and call it F.Either one works.
DE = AB, DF = AC, EF = BC, so triangle DEF ≅ triangle ABC.SSS. The other crossing gives a flipped copy that is also congruent.

geo.prompt: Copy a triangle by SSS (adapted from Construction 5, Jacobs p. 171).

steps.step: Draw a ray and mark DE equal to AB.
Draw a circle centered at D with radius AC.
Draw a circle centered at E with radius BC.
Pick one crossing point and call it F.
DE = AB, DF = AC, EF = BC, so triangle DEF ≅ triangle ABC.
steps.reason: SSS. The other crossing gives a flipped copy that is also congruent.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Copy a triangle by SAS (adapted from Constructions 3 and 4, Jacobs p. 170).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Copy AB onto DE.Compass copy of a segment.
Copy angle BAC at D, on one side of DE.Angle-copy construction.
Mark DF = AC along the new ray.Compass copy.
DE = AB, DF = AC, angle EDF = angle BAC, so triangle DEF ≅ triangle ABC.SAS. The angle copy itself works because of SSS.

geo.prompt: Copy a triangle by SAS (adapted from Constructions 3 and 4, Jacobs p. 170).

steps.step: Copy angle BAC at D, on one side of DE.
Mark DF = AC along the new ray.
DE = AB, DF = AC, angle EDF = angle BAC, so triangle DEF ≅ triangle ABC.
steps.reason: SAS. The angle copy itself works because of SSS.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Jordan measures a copy and calls it exact.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

'It looks equal' is not a reason. Name the three equal parts, then cite SSS or SAS.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
AB = 5, AC = 4, BC = 3. After DE = 5, what radii do you use?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Radius 4 at D and radius 3 at E.

Reveal second check

Each radius is the side that touches that corner.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Do the top and bottom crossing points give noncongruent copies?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. They give two distinct congruent copies. Reflection across line DE exchanges them and preserves every length; SSS applies to each.

Reveal second check

Flipping across DE swaps them.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
Can you mark a ruler reading instead of using the compass and still call it an exact construction?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. Measuring adds error and uses a different tool.

Reveal second check

Constructions copy lengths with the compass, not with numbers.

geo.title: Practice 3
geo.prompt: Can you mark a ruler reading instead of using the compass and still call it an exact construction?
geo.solution: No. Measuring adds error and uses a different tool.
geo.check: Constructions copy lengths with the compass, not with numbers.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html:
After copying AB, how many arcs do you need to locate the third vertex by SSS?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Two: one from each end, with radii equal to the other two sides.

Reveal second check

Name the givens and the theorem or definition used.
